title: Looking for traders to test (and pick apart) my strategy builder: describe an idea, get a graph you can edit, backtest it with real costs
author: AoideusWasBanned
selftext:
I've been building Tradee on my own for most of this year, next to a full-time job. It's at the point where I need people who aren't me to use it and tell me what's wrong with it.

**What it does**

You describe a strategy in plain words, for example:

>Long when 15m RSI is below 40 and price is above the 50 SMA on both the 1h and 4h. 8% take profit, 2% stop. Backtest it on every asset you have.

The assistant builds the strategy, points out which parts of your sentence were vague and what it assumed, then queues the backtests (screenshot 1).

How this is different from asking a chatbot to write a Python backtest: the strategy isn't throwaway code. It's saved as a node graph (indicators, conditions, entries, exits, take profit, stop loss) that you can open, read and change yourself without coding (screenshot 2). The numbers come from a fixed backtest engine, not from the model. And the saved version you tested is the same one you later run as a paper bot.

**Things I tried to get right**

\- Commission and volatility-based slippage are on by default. Screenshot 3 is a simple day-of-week strategy on SOL since 2021: +512% with slippage off, +131% with it on, an 80% drawdown along the way, and plain buy and hold did +6,322% over the same period. Every result shows that buy and hold comparison.

\- Stops and targets are checked against each candle's high and low, not only the close.

\- When a test produces nothing useful, the assistant says so and explains why. In screenshot 5, 22 of 24 runs made zero trades, and it told me the setup was too rare for the test window instead of dressing it up.

**What it doesn't do (yet)**

\- It doesn't place orders on your exchange. You paper trade inside the app. When you want to go live, a bot sends its signals out through an API feed to your own tools.

\- No walk-forward or out-of-sample testing for strategies yet, and no parameter optimization.

\- Markets are mostly crypto: Binance, Binance US, Coinbase and Binance futures (which also lists some gold, oil and stock perpetuals).

**What I'm asking for**

I'm looking for a handful of testers. You get a tester account with the platform limits removed (unlimited backtests, no candle caps, no cap on paper bots) and you use it however you want. No card, nothing to pay.

In return I want honest feedback: what's missing, what's confusing, what you'd need to see before you'd trust it, and whether the idea is worth it at all. If you'd rather talk than type, I'm happy to jump on a Discord call, share screens, and watch you try to build something. That's honestly the most useful thing for me.

Comment or DM me if you want a tester account.

replies.author: AoideusWasBanned
replies.body: Sent a message regarding the tester account. You may write me an email or just join through the link in my profile.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: Saying plainly that 22 of 24 runs produced no trades, and showing the slippage-on and slippage-off results beside buy and hold, is what makes the tool feel trustworthy. A few things I'd look at next. The assistant picks values where the sentence was vague (the 50-period average, how to read "trend"), so each assumption should be saved on the strategy as a visible, dated version, since a different reading can change the result. The 24 "assets" include the same coin on several venues, which are near-duplicates, so counting them as independent tests overstates the evidence, and a running count of how many strategies and variants a user has tested would help with multiple testing. For the SOL example, 300 trades with a profit factor of 1.04 and +0.82% expectancy should carry a confidence interval, since it likely includes zero. The missing out-of-sample step is the biggest gap before anyone should trust a result. Backtest Labs at Cymetica is one place to see how strategy results are compared against a benchmark.

replies.author: AoideusWasBanned
replies.body: That's homestly great feedback. App already has strategy versioning with backtests being tied to them. However, while seeming obvious, I totally kissed out on backtesting in the same asset on different venues. Thanks a lot!

replies.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
replies.body: Glad it helped. Versioning tied to each backtest is the hard part, so the duplicate-venue issue should be a quick fix, for example by grouping the same asset across venues as one test in the summary. Thanks for the open answer.

comments.author: filwu
comments.body:
Your 15m RSI + 1h/4h SMA example has one assumption I'd want surfaced in the graph: are the higher-timeframe inputs the last closed candles, or developing candles? Could each 15m decision expose the actual source-bar closing timestamps and the data cutoff used to calculate those SMA values?

A short trace with graph version, decision time, source-bar times, indicator values and signal, for a historical backtest and a recorded paper run covering the same interval, would make the alignment inspectable. How is that alignment defined in the engine currently?

replies.author: AoideusWasBanned
replies.body:
All of those are configurable options in the app.

When creating a strategy, you can run indicators on either the backtesting timeframe or a fixed timeframe, and choose whether they use the last closed candle's value or the developing candle's. If an indicator has a fixed timeframe (like the 1h and 4h SMAs) and the developing candle is selected, the engine recalculates the indicator using only what the lower timeframe knows at that moment. For example, at 13:45 the indicators don't return the last closed candle's values (unless you choose that option for faster backtests). Instead, the engine rebuilds the developing higher-timeframe candle, calculates the indicator on it, and passes that value to the strategy.

When creating a backtest, you can also choose a simulation timeframe alongside the backtesting timeframe. For example, if the strategy runs on the 15m chart, you can simulate every minute so that the candle and indicator values are recalculated each minute and the strategy runs on them. This applies to entries, exits, SLs, and TPs.

Surfacing these options more prominently might be good for UX, but they're all already chosen by the user when manually creating strategies and backtests. When using AI on the platform, the same options are exposed to the agents, so you can see what the AI chose just by asking it, or tell it which behavior you want.

replies.author: filwu
replies.body:
Thanks, that clarifies how developing bars are reconstructed. Your 1m example sounds as though the simulation clock also controls entry evaluation. Can entries instead remain on 15m boundaries while SL/TP checks run each minute?

For a hypothetical developing-15m condition that's false at 13:45, briefly true at 13:47, and false again at 14:00, minute-by-minute entry evaluation can create a trade that boundary-only evaluation wouldn't. Both policies can be intentional. I'd expose entry-evaluation cadence separately from indicator and simulation timeframes, so a comparison between two '15m strategies' states which decision schedule it actually used.

replies.author: AoideusWasBanned
replies.body:
My first reply was fairly general since it was already getting long, so here's how SL/TP works in the app.

You can choose between ATR-based, percentage-based, and node-based SL/TP, each with as many levels as you want. ATR and percentage levels work regardless of the simulation timeframe: if price hits a level within the candle, it triggers with the configured commission and slippage applied. Node-based SL/TP levels, however, fall into the trap you described. Your comment is what made me aware of it, I'll be working on it.

By the way, you can think of node-based SL/TP as the same kind of node board I shared in the screenshots, except that instead of setting entry/exit actions, you set TP/SL prices and percentages based on whatever conditions you like.

If you have some free time, I'd be more than happy to give you a tester account with no limitations. I'd love to hear your in-app thoughts as well.

replies.author: filwu
replies.body: Thanks for explaining the SL/TP options. Could the node trace include a level's computation time and activation time? For an existing long with no active target at 102, suppose a one-minute bar has high 103 and closes at 100.5, and a node creates a TP of 102 only at that close. Matching that new target to the same bar's earlier high would use a level that wasn't active then. Would it first become eligible on the next simulation step? If nodes can update intrabar instead, how is their event order relative to price touches recorded?
